title: Enabling Unstructured Sparse Fine-Tuning and Inference for Foundation Models on Wafer-Scale Engine
problem: Foundation models fine-tuned on dense weights don't benefit from sparse pre-training; dense fine-tuning negates sparsity savings, requiring full-precision inference despite underlying sparse structure.
motivation: Downstream task adaptation (fine-tuning) on sparse pre-trained models should preserve sparsity to reduce inference cost; Cerebras wafer-scale engine efficiently handles unstructured sparsity.
method: Phoenix merges sparse pre-trained weights with low-rank adapters during fine-tuning. Preserves sparsity structure while adapting to downstream tasks. Leverages Cerebras CS-2 unstructured sparsity support for efficient inference.
key_novelty: First method to maintain sparsity during fine-tuning via sparse-weight + low-rank adapter merging; enables 50–60% sparsity on Cerebras without accuracy loss.
contributions: Sparse weight + low-rank adapter merging for sparsity-preserving fine-tuning
Demonstrated unstructured sparse inference on Cerebras CS-2
Near 2× FLOP reduction at 50–60% sparsity with maintained accuracy
1.7× inference throughput improvement vs A100 GPU
limitations: Comparison limited to A100; Cerebras cost not discussed; scalability to larger models unclear; applicability to other sparse pre-training methods not evaluated.
primary_theme: Sparse inference for fine-tuned foundation models on wafer-scale
